notes.content:

Something of a major update today, SFXEngine now works in 64-bit.

-Full conversion to 64-bit. This means a 10-20% speed increase and access to full memory footprint, permitting much larger projects.
-New V02 file format for projects and programs. V00 and V01 format files will import seamlessly. There are slight technical differences between formats due to improved timing accuracy with each subsequent format. As with every format change, files saved here won't load in older versions of SFXEngine.
-All engines recompiled in 64-bit and V02 format.
-Modulator maximum size increased to match the virtually unlimited maximum sample size.
-More preparations for multi-language support.

Full details in the Readme.txt file. The next SFXEngine release will be the Fantasy Sound Pack.

notes.title: SFXEngine Updated to v2.00
notes.content:
A major SFXEngine update is live today. SFXEngine v2.00 has a bunch of new features for new sound creation and batch audio processing. There's a new look, and about 25% of the core code has been rewritten. New features include:

-New sample structure with double pointers, permitting samples beyond 90 seconds and up to several hours (as memory permits).
-New double modulator pointers for increased accuracy.
-New global sample rate option to change the core program frequency. Projects and sounds remain compatible between sample rates and will automatically resample and remap, but all filters will need manual adjustment if resampling.
-New V01 file format for projects and programs. V00 format files will import seamlessly.
-New dynamically allocated floatutility and longutility variables for engines.
-New global transpose and tuning.
-New Revision number per project, incremented upon each save.
-Improved batch csv export to prevent infinite loops, and report if no files are found.
-Improved main wav loader to skip cue chunks.
-New Locate Usage option for samples and modulators will count all uses, and locate the next use, of the current sample or modulator.
-Lots of little bug fixes and improvements.

And more! The complete Bolt-On Bundle is live today too, with a 50% discount when purchasing all Bolt-On DLC. This will prepare the way for new preset/resource packs in 2025.

notes.title: SFXEngine Updated to v1.34
notes.content:
A new update to SFXEngine is now live. Lots of interesting changes here:

-Automatic resampling of samples to allow seamless loading of non-44100hz samples.
-Silence (zerosample) level and length now settable via the Project Menu to allow dynamic changes, inc. enable/disable.
-Fix to the linear sample interpolation, added cubic Hermite interpolation, and interpolation settings added to the Sample Menu.

One big change it that the demo now includes all DLC and DLC examples to demonstrate these important effects. In the demo, DLC engines are brown and labelled "(DLC)" to clearly differentiate them from the basic engines.

-Better dynamic resizing of sound list, engine list, environment list as used in Argus.
-The start of unlinking the system to 44100hz. A new start-up procedure and background options to unify the system to a potential new rate.
-Unified WAVEFORMAT structures, default buffer size set to 32768, and lots of other smaller changes.

Enjoy creating,

Mark

notes.title: Argus Released
notes.content:
Hello All!

Our new animation software for Windows, Argus is out now. Argus uses 3D hardware and game technology to create animations in lightning-fast time.

The aim of Argus was to create a system where 3D objects (Actors) can be started and moved as quickly and easily as game sprites. Actors can be programmed move in exact ways using modulators attached to any axis of movement (or angle, or scale, or alpha transparency, and more...). If you need precise control, you can place objects in exact places on exact frames, and you can even use the mouse to move objects in real-time, recording exact movements.

Argus is free to use with limitations only to the quantity of tracks and frames. DLC can be purchased to expand tracks and frames to maximum. Find it here:
https://store.steampowered.com/app/3017550/Argus/

Argus is great tool for music videos, and it ships with templates for creating Spotify Canvas animations.

Happy animating!

Mark

notes.title: Gunstorm Released
notes.content:
Thunderstorms are rising! Our latest game, the space shooter Gunstorm is released today.

Gunstorm is a rotary, arena space-shooter that (by default) uses mouse left/right movements to rotate your ship, giving your craft huge manoeuvrability. You can also play with a 'follow the cursor' mouse mode, or using an X-Box 360 style game controller, or the keyboard if you prefer.

The plot is simple. Xodar of Gorn, in his vast battle-station, challenges you to 100 levels of alien craft. Each level has more enemies which appear faster. Each enemy reacts and moves in a different way. There are different level types too, from a level like arcade classic Asteroids where rocks are blasted into smaller and smaller chunks, to levels with static gun turrets, motherships and end-of-level guardians, and more surprises to discover.

You can choose a fixed or random level layout, and set the game speed, to make it as easy or as hard as you want. As well as the normal game you can choose to play stand-alone Asteroids, or the 'Onslaught' game featuring one huge level of different enemies. Gunstorm features games continues, automatically saves progress and settings in Steam Cloud, and awards a Steam Achievement if you defeat Xodar.

Gunstorm includes the classic theme music 'Deflexion', plus an optional remix of the 2007 Gunstorm song sung by Tor James Faulker. The Gunstorm EP (published by Cornutopia Music) includes several 1980s-style electronic pop tunes, and will be released on Steam as DLC in due course.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2787740/Gunstorm/

Enjoy battling Xodar!

Mark

notes.title: SFXEngine Released!
notes.content:
Our premiere sound effects software, SFXEngine, is now released.

SFXEngine is the fastest and most flexible way to create and manage new sounds. All of the Cornutopia Games, and countless others over the last 15 years, have used SFXEngine to create their sound effects. Now for the first time, this software is available to anyone, from game developers, to film makers, to musicians.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2438590/SFXEngine/

SFXEngine uses a row of sound processors that are applied simply one to another in a chain. This is how many software synthesizers work but SFXEngine is different in that it removes complex signal chains, and is optimised for single pitches rather than music. Any parameter of every engines, from filter frequencies, to saw-wave pitches, to sample volumes can be modulated by attaching a waveform to it. These modulator waves are wav files themselves, allowing lots of editing potential.

The program has a free-to-try demo with full editing capabilities, and as part of this release, some classic sound effects from Cornutopia Games will be made public on https://marksheeky.itch.io shortly so people can play around with those sounds.

Happy playing,

Mark

notes.title: SFXEngine Coming Soon
notes.content:
Time to make a first announcement!

The next Cornutopia release will be SFXEngine, unique audio creation software for creating sound effects. All of the sound effects for the Cornutopia Games were created using SFXEngine, and sound effects for many other commercial game titles from PC to Nintendo 3DS, as well as most of the 13,000 strong IndieSFX game sound effects library.

The key to SFXEngine's power is ease of use. It uses a modular chain of sound processors, termed Engines, to quickly layer sounds. Any parameter of any engine can be changed at whim, or transformed over time using a modulator, which in the case of SFXEngine is a simple wav file itself, so it's easy to design complex envelopes and oscillators without the complexity of editing ADSR envelopes.

Optimised for monotone sound effects, unlike music synthesizers, SFXEngine acts as a creation tool and a librarian for groups of sound effects.

The store page is here:
https://store.steampowered.com/app/2438590/SFXEngine/

SFXEngine is high-end audio production software, with all unique audio algorithms and internal 32-bit processing throughout, but will be targeted at game developers at every level.

SFXEngine will launch on June 23rd at $75, including a 25% launch discount.

notes.title: Everything About Taskforce
notes.content:
Hi, I'm Mark Sheeky. I'm surrealist oil painter and music artist now but I've been making games for most of my life, since the 80s back on a Dragon 32 and later Commodore 64.

My Steam Games Festival game Taskforce is the latest in a long line of turn-based, squad-level strategy games I've made. Back in 1993 I made a game called Taskforce for Amiga featuring a team of elite soldiers tasked with completing a special mission. A few years later I released Hilt II, a far more advanced game which is still popular today, then in 1999, a CD-based isometric PC game called Arcangel. Taskforce: The Mutants of October Morgane is the latest in this 25-year evolution of this sort of game and is fully 3D, and uses my own custom-designed game engine called HECToR.

You are cast as commander of Teuton Arcanum Special Knight Force, and given command of 12 elite soldiers to complete a series of mission which unfold to tell a complete story. You'll fight different enemies in different terrains, and choose how to equip them for your own tactics.

I wanted the game to be very open, non-linear, and give the player a chance to play each mission lots of times while making each game different. The start positions for targets and enemy soldiers (or monsters) are random each time, and many of the map layouts are random too. Each mission can be completed in lots of different ways, there is no single path; it's up to you to work out how you want to complete the mission. There are four difficulty levels too, and this setting changes the mission parameters in unique ways for each mission, making the game different every time.

There are 16 main story missions, plus 16 training missions which unlock as you progress through the game, and any past mission can be played as many times as you like. Taskforce also includes a detailed manual which will be published and optionally purchasable as a book from Amazon.

In Taskforce I wanted to make a game which reflects the best of the 80s and 90s Microprose games that I loved to play, games like Project Stealth Fighter and Airborne Ranger, where the time you invest in each mission and each game is rewarded. I wanted to make a game that was realistic, and open, not a fixed path or puzzle, but something like a simulation to play with time and time again.

The game demo will be available from June 9th 2020 and the full game will be released on July 24th 2020.

notes.title: Taskforce Dev Update: Training Testing
notes.content:
A few tweaks to the game today and testing the new training missions. All have new objectives. The Assassination Training involves hunting one enemy but not being allowed to kill anyone except your target. It's perfect for one, lone unit, hiding behind objects and using stealth tactics. The opposite end is the Major Assault, one of the few missions in the game which allows you to use all 12 members of the squad. In this, an overwhelming force, more than 3:1, have taken over your base and you must retake it.

Testing is taking place each day. We're at the stage now where radical new ideas are for potential sequels. The key thing now is to check that what is there, and what should be there, works exactly as it should.

Most of the training missions make use of multiple levels to provide interesting vantage points. This Terror Troop armed with a Pyrox Burner is one of 40 enemies here.

notes.title: Taskforce Dev Update: Teuton Arcanum
notes.content:
Great progress on Taskforce. You can see all new screenshots of the latest build on the store today. I can now introduce Teuton Arcanum, the organisation you will command in the game.

The Teuton Arcanum Special Knight Force, known as Taskforce, is a global organisation, founded in the 9th century in Aachen, Germany, by executive order of Emperor Charlemagne. It originally consisted of nine trusted knights, and indeed even today it is led by the 'Nine Unknown Knights'; unknown because even the Knights themselves do not know the real identities of the other members.

The organisation has survived until today, and is now based in a underground city beneath the Swiss Alps known as The Cathedral. Their symbol is the Arcanum Knot, a nine pointed star, and each point represents one of the Nine Unknown Knights and the different departments which they administer: Archival, Scientific, Esoteric, Political, Active Scientific and Practical Operations (ASPO makes all of your equipment), Sentinel, Financial, Military, and the Dark Order.

In the game you will command Knight Force One, twelve of the 169 troops in the Military wing.

notes.title: Taskforce Dev Update: New Graphics System
notes.content:
A huge few weeks for Taskforce. A week ago I decided to reprogram the graphics system entirely, which needed new versions of the 400-or-so objects in the game. At the same time, I thought I'd create new textures at double the existing resolution too, so effectively all of the terrain graphics have been recreated in the past, long and exhausting, week.

Now, blocks and wall sections are correctly sealed, effectively automatically creating tubes of polygons for the walls and windows etc. Before, almost all objects showed strange fragments of polygons, holes, gaps. Everything looked like an error, but was there for speed. Now it's probably faster and looks better. Here is a look:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37538589/789b2e5cec51087a90790055d809f0e7bf3c275f.jpg[/img]

Those concrete-ends are just the unseen walls, the black holes will be filled in when your troops see them, as normal. One other thing is that you can now shoot through windows, which looks great and allows proper S.A.S. style entry into buildings.

All of this work means that, sadly, I won't be able to make the deadline for the Steam Summer Games Festival. A public demo will appear, but not this week. Due to the busy-ness of Steam's June Fest, the release date for Taskforce might be pushed back to the end of July.

One last note is that now that all of the graphics are new, the existing screenshots and the video are effectively invalid. I will create new ones...

notes.title: Taskforce Dev Update: Commando Fun
notes.content:
Huge updates to Taskforce today. I've added the ability to skip units which have moved, and restricted movement on top of odd tiles, like walking over pot-plants, this was actually possible! I've also added a lot more music options. Oddly, for me, there isn't much music in this game; I'd like to add more but time is so limited.

At least five of the missions have had big changes to the maps. I want to make everything non-linear, so that players are given a target but can do it in so many ways that there is no right or wrong or best way. In this mission, a tiny commando-style raid has been authorised; you take just 4 units and must enter a building at night with the aim of destroying a cluster of generators. You are massively outnumbered by armed guards, so must evade as much as possible. There are so many ways in and out of the building that you are free to choose. You can even walk right over the roof and enter the target zone itself without so much as a single guard. All a far cry from linear F.P.S. games with a start here and a target at the end of the hall, but of course, no route is necessarily best, and, just as in [i]The Guns of Navarone[/i], you must escape after the bombs go off.

notes.title: Taskforce Dev Update: Training Missions
notes.content:
Working hard today on new training missions. These are a big part of the game, each new unlocked mission also unlocks training missions, allowing you to face enemies in a sort of holodeck environment. I'm designing new maps for each type of training. My golden rule is to give the player options. These games are more like multiplayer F.P.S. games than most single player games. Every game different, with so many options and missions to choose from that you can play again and again and never have the same experience.

Here's a look at the one of them in testing (no secrets to which!) - the special thing about this one is that your team starts separated, and in a different place each time you play.
